statement: Can rank-1 blocks that are not stars give rank(A) ≥ 22 on the 41-row domain? This is the question the star lemma cannot answer. The König argument breaks because a rank-1 support can be a rectangle with a large cover, and zeroing entries outside R_j can increase rank, so there is no simple subadditivity bound by k. The next experiment should search rank-1 blocks directly and test whether the bound stays ≤ k or grows. It should also test whether a block with a rectangular support can carry more rank than a star. That decides whether option (1) is open or ruled out.

structure.why: At n=12,14,16 the mean ratio K_l/2^l at l=n-4 is 0.86, 0.77, 0.53 on 6 to 10 random samples. statement: Backlog repair for the stage decomposition of S0016/S0017 fails. Counterexample (hand argument, N = 2^m, u >= 2): t_1(x) = N*u/2 and t_i(x) = 1 for 2 <= i <= N-1, so sum_i t_i = N*u/2 + N - 1 <= N*u. Carrying unfinished interval-1 steps forward spreads them over stages 1..N/2, each stage running u steps with no input read. Bit x_j arrives in stage j (its fixed wire) but is consumed only after interval 1 ends, around stage N/2. So about N/2 input bits are pending at the same stage, and the carried state is Theta(N) bits, not poly(S*w). The backlog is therefore not O(1) under t_i >= 1 and sum_i t_i <= N*u, which answers the open question from the previous turn negatively. Consequence: under the amortised reading of MMW Thm 1.2 (sum_i t_i <= N*u), neither the per-stage repair S0016(a) nor the backlog repair gives Lemma 12 (Gamma <= 2^m*poly(s)). Lemma 12 needs the per-interval worst-case reading, so G0002 stays the decisive gap. Not checked by the lab; no cross-family review; no verdict recorded.

At n=6 every minimal core has degree exactly 2 (3477 cores). Test at n=7,8,9 on random and extremal unsat families (monomials 2^n, so linear algebra is cheap), and check whether any minimal core reaches degree 3. Implication: a constant bound d would give a degree-d linear-algebra decision procedure of size O(n^d) for UNSAT, i.e. coNP in P and so P=NP along this route. Growing degree on a family is a limit of this method only, not of all algorithms.

Theorem 1.4 (Section 5) verbatim: for s(n) >= n and A in PH, (i) if there is eps > 0 such that for all c >= 1, search-MCSP^A[2^(eps n/c)] on inputs of length N = 2^n has no N^(1+eps)-size O(1/eps)-depth TC0 circuits, then NP is not contained in TC0; (ii) if search-MCSP^A[s(n)] has no N*poly(s(n))-size O(log N)-depth circuits then NP is not in NC1; (iii) if search-MCSP^A[s(n)] has no N*poly(s(n))-size poly(s(n))-depth circuits then NP is not in P/poly. Row B's TC0 hypothesis matches bullet (i) exactly, so its numbering is CONFIRMED as Theorem 1.4. CORRECTION: the earlier record that attributed the TC0 bullet to Theorem 1.7 was wrong; Theorem 1.7 in MMW19 is the MKTP consequence list. Row B is verified as a statement only. Row B's obstacle is the hypothesis itself: a TC0 circuit lower bound for search-MCSP^A is not known, so row B yields a conditional implication, not progress. Rows A, E, F, G remain unverified.

structure.content: Source check of MMW19 Thm 1.4 (people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf, web_read offset 13500). Thm 1.4 (A in PH, s >= n) has three bullets: (i) if for some eps>0 and all c>=1, search-MCSP^A[2^{eps n/c}] on N=2^n has no N^{1+eps}-size O(1/eps)-depth TC0 circuits, then NP not in TC0; (ii) if search-MCSP^A[s] has no N*poly(s)-size O(log N)-depth circuits, then NP not in NC1; (iii) if search-MCSP^A[s] has no N*poly(s)-size poly(s)-depth circuits, then NP not in P/poly (hence P != NP). CORRECTION to contract row B: MMW19 Thm 1.4 is NOT a formula-simulation theorem; it has no exponent c<1 for circuit-to-formula simulation. Row B's P!=NP route is only bullet (iii). Its gap is a lower bound against N*poly(s)-size poly(s)-depth circuits for search-MCSP^A[s], A in PH, s>=n. The paper itself says even O(N)-size O(log N)-depth lower bounds are open, so row B is not closer than the open problem. Not checked here: Thm 1.1 and 1.2 proofs (Sections 3-4).
